clue.text: Underwear piles — the basic facts

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear; plural here
piles and stacks are both heaps of things

explanation.surface: Heaps of lingerie are presented as the plain truth of the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the fundamentals is the idiom 'getting down to brass tacks', so the phrase names the essential details.

clue.text: Predict how violin may be played on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a violin is played with a bow, so it may be bowed

explanation.surface: A forecast about how a violin performance will be broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To bode is to foretell or portend, as in 'this bodes well'.

clue.text: Friends quietly sliding down mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter slides lower, so it moves to the end

parts.note: pals are friends
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A group of friends silently sledging down some mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliding down' moves P from the top of PALS to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe; the word is also used for any high mountains.

clue.text: Perhaps Eccles is one found in a jam

definitions.text: Perhaps Eccles is one found in a jam

parts.words: Perhaps Eccles is one found in a jam
parts.note: Eccles sets this crossword, so is a setter and agent of it; pectin is what sets jam

explanation.walkthrough: Eccles, this puzzle's setter, sets crosswords; pectin, the substance that makes jam set, has the same description. 'Eccles' also suggests the Eccles cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the classic jelling substance in jam, and a crossword compiler is jokingly an agent who sets puzzles.

clue.text: Claims Republican seizes belongings? On the contrary

indicators.note: seizing something holds it, so one piece is placed inside another
this reverses the roles just stated, so the belongings hold the party letter rather than the other way round

parts.note: assets are things a person owns

explanation.surface: A political accusation that a Republican has grabbed someone's property, then contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizes' with 'On the contrary' means ASSETS takes in R, not R taking in ASSETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserts and claims both mean states something firmly as true.

clue.text: Relative regularly appearing in bikini contest's magazine

indicators.note: taking letters at a steady interval, here every third one, through the following words

explanation.surface: A family member keeps turning up in a magazine's swimsuit-contest pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A kinsman is a male blood relation, a member of one's family.

clue.text: Take clothes off to portray heroic tale

indicators.note: stripping someone of clothes removes the outer layer, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: to portray something is to depict it

explanation.surface: A performer stripping off in order to act out a hero's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take clothes off' strips the outer letters D and T from DEPICT, leaving the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem or saga celebrating the deeds of a legendary hero.

clue.text: Drop an ugly oddball outside part of school?

indicators.note: an oddball is strange, and here the ball of letters is mixed oddly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop an unattractive misfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddball' signals the anagram; 'outside' belongs to the definition, not a containment.
explanation.definitionFit: The outdoor area where pupils play at break is the open-air section of a school's grounds.

clue.text: Worries about muck up by German magazines

indicators.note: one word goes about the others, enclosing them

parts.note: cares are worries

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: dirt is muck

explanation.surface: Anxieties about a German stirring up filth, in some magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means read bottom to top. 'magazines' here means ammunition holders for guns, not periodicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is also the container of ammunition loaded into a gun, and cartridges are such units.

clue.text: Standing in bit of iguana dung, I step awkwardly

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly suggests clumsy disorder, so these letters are rearranged
a small bit of the word is just its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recounting how they clumsily trod in lizard droppings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' gives the I from iguana; 'awkwardly' shuffles it with DUNG, I and STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputising is acting as a substitute for someone else, which is what standing in for them means.

clue.text: Independent, boring, average couple

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, so this letter goes inside the word

parts.note: par is a normal or average level

explanation.surface: A dull, middling pair of people who happen to be unaffiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' puts I inside PAR. 'boring' and 'average' look like adjectives describing the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple and a pair are synonyms, both meaning two of something taken together.

clue.text: Influential piece of music

definitions.meaning: being ... in an outcome means playing an important part in it
a track played on instruments without singing

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for having a key role in bringing something about and a noun for a vocal-free tune.

clue.text: Grimace unhappily around Italian control freak

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the other piece, enclosing it
a word put together unhappily is badly arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, from Italy's capital

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a sour face at an Italian who insists on controlling everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' shuffles the first word into MICAGER, which then goes 'around' the Italian; 'Grimace' looks like a verb but is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A micromanager supervises every small detail of others' work, the typical behaviour of a controlling personality.

clue.text: Undecided where to put creosote?

definitions.meaning: sitting undecided means not taking sides
creosote is a wood preservative painted on garden boarding, the location being the timber barrier

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for neutrality pictures sitting astride a dividing barrier, and literally a garden barrier is where wood preservative is brushed.

clue.text: Unexceptional claims: Tory leader meaning the opposite

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so it goes inside

parts.note: anonymous can mean lacking distinctive features, nondescript

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bland pronouncements from a Conservative chief that mean the reverse of what they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims' looks like a noun here but is a verb: ANONYMOUS takes in T, the first of Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonymous describes words that are antonyms, having opposite senses.

clue.text: Minorities in Norway working a long time

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway
a machine that is on is working
ages means a long time, as in 'I waited for ages'

explanation.surface: Minority communities in Norway have been employed there for many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonage is the legal state of being under age, so the plural names periods of legal minority, not small groups.

clue.text: Make my daughter serve again after this?

parts.note: to net a sum is to make it as profit
'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent instructing a daughter to have another go at serving, perhaps at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make my daughter' reads like a command; it is three pieces. COR is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve clipping the top of the net and landing in is a let, so the server takes it again.

clue.text: American can leave wife to follow prostitute like this, on reflection

indicators.note: these letters come after the earlier ones in the answer

parts.note: ho is slang for a prostitute

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: so means in this way, as in 'do it so'
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An American man may walk out on his wife to chase a sex worker, as he admits on thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns SO into OS. 'can' is slang for prison, not a tin or a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoosgow is American slang for a jail, and 'can' is another American slang word for prison.

clue.text: Petulant desire to drink like Penny

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a wish is a desire
as means like, as in 'dressed as a clown'

explanation.surface: A grumpy craving for a drink just like the one Penny has.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply irritable or peevish, a temperament like the stinging insect.

clue.text: Graduates' slander case dismissed by a judge, in the end

definitions.note: the definition is the plural noun for female graduates; the apostrophe stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer shell, and dismissing it removes the first and last letters

parts.note: calumny is a false and damaging statement, or slander

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Some graduates' defamation suit is thrown out by a judge at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case dismissed' looks like legal jargon in this courtroom scene; it removes C and Y from CALUMNY. 'in the end' takes E from judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumnae are former female students of a school or university, the feminine plural of the Latin alumnus.

clue.text: A star of French Resistance is torn

parts.note: the Sun is a star
de is French for 'of'
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A heroine of the French wartime underground is emotionally torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Resistance' reads as the wartime movement, but splits into 'of French' and 'Resistance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn asunder means ripped apart into pieces, so the adverb describes something split.

clue.text: A curse from this UFO?

parts.note: the second word, read as an anagram signal, sends the letters of the word for crockery flying into the words 'a curse'

explanation.surface: Someone shouts an oath at the sight of an unidentified object in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'flying' is an anagram signal and SAUCER rearranges into A CURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc-shaped craft supposedly piloted by aliens is the popular image of an unidentified object in the sky.

clue.text: Experts listened to ordinary language

indicators.note: something listened to is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: prose is ordinary written or spoken language, not verse

explanation.surface: Specialists paid attention to everyday speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros are professionals, people skilled and paid in their field.

clue.text: Confusion as leading goal-scorer fails to finish

indicators.note: failing to finish loses the last letter

parts.note: Lionel Messi, the Argentine footballer, is one of the top scorers in history

explanation.surface: Chaos ensues when the star striker misses his chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' fits the football scene but removes the I from MESSI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of disorder or muddle.

clue.text: One repeatedly has trapped gas?

indicators.note: only what is trapped inside is kept, so the outer letters of the doubled word fall away
repeating the word gives it twice in a row

explanation.surface: Someone keeps suffering from wind, a mildly comic complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles ONE to ONEONE; 'has trapped' keeps only what lies inside, dropping the outer O and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, the element that glows red in advertising signs.

clue.text: Frenchman welcomes romantic meeting in apartment

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
a date is a romantic meeting

explanation.surface: A Frenchman hosts a lovers' rendezvous in his flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small flat or lodging kept for occasional use, usually in a city.

clue.text: Stop scratching head for relaxation

indicators.note: scratching out the head of a word deletes its first letter

parts.note: to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: Quit clawing at your scalp and you will feel more at peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' looks like an itchy habit; it removes C from CEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of comfort and rest, free from strain, which is what relaxation brings.

clue.text: Brief leans over catalogues of candidates

parts.note: brief and short are synonyms
a ship that lists leans over to one side

explanation.surface: A short note tilts across a set of catalogues, an odd office scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortlists are selected sets of the strongest applicants from which a final choice is made.
